diagnosis: The issue lies in how the tokenizer handles semicolons as comment starters. When a semicolon is encountered at the beginning of input, the code fails to correctly identify and process it as a comment token, leading to incorrect subsequent tokenization.

causal_chain: The `get_token` function (lines 146-197) mishandles semicolon comments by not properly reading until the end of the line or file.
In `is_token_end`, comment handling (str_com_id=2) only ends on newline, causing incomplete tokenization.

repair_candidates.assumption: Modify `get_token` to correctly read until newline or EOF for comments.

edits.rationale: Handle comment end on newline or EOF.

repair_candidates.expected_effect: Properly tokenize comments until newline or EOF, preventing incorrect subsequent tokens.

repair_candidates.assumption: Adjust `is_token_end` to recognize EOF as a comment end condition.

edits.rationale: Ensure comments end on newline or EOF.

repair_candidates.expected_effect: Correctly terminate comments at EOF, allowing proper tokenization of subsequent inputs.
preservation_constraints: Maintain existing comment handling for non-EOF cases
repair_candidates.repair_intent: Modify `is_token_end` to handle EOF in comments.

repair_candidates.assumption: Enhance buffer management in `get_token` for comment tokens.

edits.rationale: Ensure all characters up to newline or EOF are read for comments.
